GovTech is almost fully funded from (a) central grants from the Government and (b) other Government agencies paying for the use of GovTech’s services and products. This is unlikely to change significantly in the near future.

reports.title: Active Monitoring/Alert System to Detect Oil Spillage to Ensure More Effective and Expedient Recovery Efforts
reports.mp_names: Mr Chee Hong Tat,Ms Joan Pereira

turns.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
turns.text: asked the Minister for Transport regarding the oil leakage from a Shell land-based pipeline between Bukom Island and Bukom Kecil on 20 October 2024 (a) whether an active monitoring or alert system is in place to detect oil sightings in Singapore’s water; and (b) what are the lessons and experiences from previous oil leaks and spills that the Government is applying to ensure that the recovery efforts are more effective and expedient.

turns.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
turns.text: I thank the Member for the Question. This Question has been addressed in the reply to Question Nos 7 and 8 for Oral Answer at the 11 November 2024 Sitting. [Please refer to "Inspection for Structural Integrity of Oil Pipelines, Measures to Prevent Oil Spills and Penalties for Recent Incidents", Official Report, 11 November 2024, Vol 95, Issue 145, Oral Answers to Questions section.]

reports.report_type: Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer Not Answered by End of Question Time
reports.title: Installation of Lifts at Overhead Bridges in Fernvale for Benefit of Seniors and Families with Young Children
reports.mp_names: Mr Gan Thiam Poh,Mr Chee Hong Tat

turns.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
turns.text: asked the Minister for Transport whether LTA will consider installing lifts at overhead bridges in Fernvale for the benefit of seniors and families with young children.

turns.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
turns.text: Since 2018, all new pedestrian overhead bridges (POBs) are installed with lifts to provide barrier-free access. The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has also been retrofitting some POBs built before 2018 with lifts. We have focused on POBs near Mass Rapid Transit stations, bus interchanges and healthcare institutions, such as hospitals and polyclinics. These POBs experience higher footfall and serve more seniors. Priority is also being given to POBs without nearby street-level or alternative barrier-free pedestrian crossings. In Fernvale, LTA has included the POB along Sengkang West Way near Blk 469B under its lift retrofitting programme. LTA will continue to assess other POBs in Fernvale for lift retrofitting.

reports.report_type: Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer Not Answered by End of Question Time
reports.title: Feasibility of Extending MediShield Life Coverage to Include Maternity Charges
reports.mp_names: Mr Ong Ye Kung,Mr Leong Mun Wai

turns.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
turns.text: asked the Minister for Health whether Medishield Life coverage can be extended to include maternity charges so as to reduce a financial burden on expecting parents.

turns.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
turns.text: As MediShield Life is a basic health insurance scheme which protects Singaporeans against large subsidised medical bills arising from accidents or illnesses, general maternity expenses are not covered by MediShield Life. Instead, the Government provides subsidies of up to 80% for maternity expenses, and MediSave use through the MediSave Maternity Package. MediShield Life coverage does kick in for the treatment of serious pregnancy and delivery-related complications. Beyond subsidies for maternity expenses, the Government also provides significant additional support for parents, such as the Baby Bonus Cash Gift, and the MediSave Grant for Newborns, which will be increased from $4,000 to $5,000 from 1 April 2025.

reports.report_type: Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer Not Answered by End of Question Time
reports.title: Additional Direct Bus Services by Private Operators for Residents in Fernvale to CBD During Peak Hours
reports.mp_names: Mr Gan Thiam Poh,Mr Chee Hong Tat

turns.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
turns.text: asked the Minister for Transport whether the Ministry will consider allowing private bus operators to provide direct connection bus services for residents in Fernvale to and from the Central Business District (CBD) during the morning and evening peak periods as residents still find that the additional trips by SBS Transit City Direct Bus Service 671 to and from CBD not quite sufficient.

turns.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
turns.text: The Land Transport Authority welcomes private bus operators to operate additional bus services to complement our public transport services and provide more travel options for the residents. Besides City Direct Service 671, Fernvale residents are presently served by the privately-operated Premium Bus Services 550 and 592 to the Central Business District. Residents may access these bus services along Sengkang West Avenue, Sengkang West Way or Jalan Kayu.

reports.report_type: Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer Not Answered by End of Question Time
reports.title: Plans to Increase EV-charging Lots in HDB Car Parks with High Population of EVs Registered for Season Parking
reports.mp_names: Dr Lim Wee Kiak,Mr Chee Hong Tat

turns.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
turns.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what is the current number of electric vehicles (EVs) registered for season parking in HDB carparks; and (b) whether there are plans to increase the availability of EV charging lots in HDB carparks where there is a higher number of EVs registered for season parking.

turns.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
turns.text: As of end September 2024, there are about 8,800 electric vehicles (EVs) registered with season parking at Housing and Development Board (HDB) car parks. The average EV charger utilisation rate at HDB car parks is currently under 10% and remains sufficient to meet the demand from EV drivers. We closely monitor EV charger utilisation at all HDB car parks, and work with the EV charging operators to scale up deployment of EV chargers where necessary.

reports.report_type: Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer Not Answered by End of Question Time
reports.title: Rationale for Age Restriction on Redeeming MediShield Life Premium Discounts Earned Through Healthy 365 App
reports.mp_names: Mr Ong Ye Kung,Mr Leong Mun Wai

turns.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
turns.text: asked the Minister for Health what is the rationale for excluding policyholders aged below 40 from qualifying to redeem MediShield Life premium discounts using Healthpoints that are earned through the Healthy 365 app.

turns.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
turns.text: This is a pilot project to encourage individuals to lead healthier lifestyles by allowing them to redeem their Healthpoints for discounts on their premiums. This pilot is targeted at individuals aged 40 and above because it is in support of Healthier SG, which targets the same age group. By focusing on this age group, we are also more likely to see clearer correlation between healthy lifestyles and good health and provide the evidence to consider if it can be a permanent feature of MediShield Life.

reports.report_type: Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer Not Answered by End of Question Time
reports.title: Costs Incurred by NParks in Maintenance and Treatment of Animals Seized During Investigations
reports.mp_names: Mr Desmond Lee,Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang

turns.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
turns.text: asked the Minister for National Development for each year in the past five years, what are the mean and median costs borne by the National Parks Board for the costs and expenses incurred in the maintenance and treatment of animals seized during investigations.

turns.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
turns.text: The National Parks Board (NParks) bears the costs and expenses involved in the maintenance and treatment of animals in its centres. This includes animals that have been seized during investigations, as well as those that are brought to the centres under the Trap-Neuter-Rehome/Release-Manage programme for community cats and dogs. NParks does not track the costs and expenses incurred in the maintenance and treatment of specific animals.

reports.report_type: Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer Not Answered by End of Question Time
reports.title: Effect of Removal of Mandatory Saturday Services at Childcare Centres on Wages of Educators
reports.mp_names: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye,Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M

turns.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
turns.text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development how will the Early Childhood Development Agency ensure that the wages of early childhood educators are not negatively impacted as a direct result of the removal of mandatory Saturday services at childcare centres which will come into effect from January 2025.

turns.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
turns.text: Shifting to a five-day work week serves to improve the well-being of early childhood educators and make early childhood careers more attractive and sustainable. This change should not come at the expense of educators’ wages. The total monthly working hours and wages agreed between the educators and employers should remain as stated in their current contracts, unless mutually agreed otherwise.

reports.title: Statistics of Students with Reported Special Education Needs in Mainstream Schools
reports.mp_names: Mr Chan Chun Sing,Mr Ong Hua Han

turns.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
turns.text: asked the Minister for Education in respect of mainstream school students with reported special education needs, what is the current breakdown in percentage of those who have (i) autism spectrum disorder (ii) intellectual disabilities (iii) sensory disabilities (iv) physical disabilities (v) neurodiverse conditions other than autism and (vi) multiple disabilities, respectively.

turns.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
turns.text: Among mainstream school students with special educational needs (SEN), students with dyslexia, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) make up the vast majority. Students with other disability profiles, such as sensory disabilities, physical disabilities and multiple disabilities, make up a very small percentage of mainstream school students with SEN.

reports.title: Requests for Assistance with Visa Applications by Singaporean Students Furthering Studies in Australia
reports.mp_names: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan,Ms Hany Soh

turns.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
turns.text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs in light of Australia’s plans to impose an enrolment cap on the number of international students from 2025 (a) whether the Ministry has received any requests for assistance with visa applications from Singaporean students; and (b) how can the Ministry assist and support these students, especially those who are midway through their studies at Australian universities.

turns.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
turns.text: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has not received requests for assistance from Singaporeans. The Australian government has indicated that international students who have already started their courses will not be affected by the proposed caps.

reports.report_type: Written Answers to Questions for Oral Answer Not Answered by End of Question Time
reports.title: Salary Range Monitoring on MyCareersFuture Portal to Ensure Accuracy
reports.mp_names: Dr Tan See Leng,Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan

turns.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
turns.text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether the Ministry conducts checks on MyCareersFuture portal to ensure that salary ranges for jobs listed on the portal are accurate.

turns.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
turns.text: The Ministry of Manpower does not conduct checks on the salary ranges listed in the job advertisements posted on the MyCareersFuture portal or other job portals. Companies have the flexibility to set the salary ranges for the jobs they offer and to list these in their job advertisements. The onus is on hirers to provide a fair and accurate description of the job and associated salary.

reports.title: Studies on Usefulness of Body Roundness Index as Predictor of Obesity and Related Health Risks
reports.mp_names: Mr Ong Hua Han,Mr Ong Ye Kung

turns.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han
turns.text: asked the Minister for Health whether there are any ongoing or planned studies in Singapore to explore the usefulness of body roundness index as a predictor of obesity and related health risks for the population.

turns.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
turns.text: There is currently insufficient evidence on the usefulness of Body Roundness Index as a predictor of obesity and related health risks for Asian populations. The Ministry of Health will continue to monitor research findings and, in the meantime, use predictors, such as waist circumference and body mass index, for our national screening programme.
